sentences.en: My lord of Hereford here, whom you call king, is a foul traitor to proud Hereford's king.
sentences.zh: 这里你称为国王的这位我的赫里福德勋爵，是骄傲的赫里福德国王的一个十恶不赦的叛徒。

sentences.en: And if you crown him, let me prophesy, the blood of English shall manure the ground, and future ages groan for this foul act.
sentences.zh: 如果你们为他加冕，请听我预言，英格兰人的鲜血将玷污这片土地，后世必将为这一恶行发出哀叹。

sentences.en: Peace shall go sleep with Turks and infidels, and in this seat of peace, tumultuous wars shall kin with kin and kind with kind confound.
sentences.zh: 和平将与土耳其人和异教徒同眠，在这片和平的宝座上，同胞将自相残杀，骨肉将同室操戈。

sentences.en: Disorder, horror, fear, and mutiny shall here inhabit, and this land be called the Field of Golgotha and Dead Men's Skulls.
sentences.zh: 混乱、恐惧、惊慌和兵变将在此驻留，这片土地将被称作各各他与死人头骨之野。

sentences.en: Oh, if you raise this house against this house, it will the woefulest division prove that ever fell upon this cursed earth.
sentences.zh: 哦，如果你们让这个家族骨肉相残，这将成为这片受诅咒的土地上经历过的最悲惨的分裂。

sentences.en: Prevent it, resist it, let it not be so, lest child, child's children cry against you, woe.
sentences.zh: 阻止它，抵抗它，莫让它发生，免得后代子孙对你们哭诉悲哀。

sentences.en: So that is the Bishop of Carlisle, William Shakespeare's Richard II.
sentences.zh: 这就是卡莱尔主教，威廉·莎士比亚笔下的《理查二世》。

sentences.en: And that moment, Tom, comes at the fateful moment, doesn't it?
sentences.zh: 而那一刻，汤姆，发生在那个决定命运的时刻，对吧？

sentences.en: The climax of Shakespeare's great play.
sentences.zh: 莎士比亚伟大戏剧的高潮。

sentences.en: A play that is not one of the most performed in the Shakespearean canon, but it has some of the finest writings, some of the most beautiful passages.
sentences.zh: 这部剧在莎士比亚的剧作中并不是演出的最多的一部，但它拥有一些最精彩的辞藻、一些最美妙的段落。

sentences.en: I thought you did wonderful justice to it.
sentences.zh: 我觉得你将它演绎得精彩绝伦。

sentences.en: Well, that is kind.
sentences.zh: 噢，过奖了。

sentences.en: I especially love the catch in your throat in the final few lines.
sentences.zh: 我尤其喜欢你在最后几行台词中那哽咽的嗓音。

sentences.en: Well, that's what a great actor.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这就是伟大的演员。

sentences.en: As you contemplate England turning to civil war, very, very moving, Dominic.
sentences.zh: 当你沉思英格兰陷入内战时，非常、非常感人，多米尼克。

sentences.en: It's not complicated, Tom, it's just acting.
sentences.zh: 这并不复杂，汤姆，这只是演戏。

sentences.en: I know it is.
sentences.zh: 我知道是的。

sentences.en: So that's the moment on the 1st of October, 1399, when Richard II was deposed.
sentences.zh: 这就是1399年10月1日那个理查二世被废黜的时刻。

sentences.en: He was kicked out and replaced by Henry Bolingbroke, who became Henry IV.
sentences.zh: 他被赶下台，由亨利·博林布鲁克取而代之，后者成为了亨利四世。

sentences.en: And in Shakespeare's history plays, Tom, his great cycle goes all the way through to Richard III.
sentences.zh: 在莎士比亚的历史剧里，汤姆，他伟大的历史剧周期一直延续到了理查三世。

sentences.en: Everything starts with that moment.
sentences.zh: 一切都始于那一刻。

sentences.en: That is the trigger for the Wars of the Roses, for the high drama of the 15th century, for the kind of usurpations and depositions and battles
sentences.zh: 那是玫瑰战争的导火索，是15世纪宏大戏剧的导火索，是那种篡位、废黜、战乱

sentences.en: and murders of princes in the tower and all those kinds of things.
sentences.zh: 以及塔中王子谋杀案之类事情的导火索。

sentences.en: And it's a great moment.
sentences.zh: 这是一个伟大的时刻。

sentences.en: It comes in the midpoint of the Hundred Years' War.
sentences.zh: 它正处于百年战争的中点。

sentences.en: So you've done a mighty series on that.
sentences.zh: 所以你为此做了一个宏大的系列节目。

sentences.en: And this is often seen as a kind of turning point, certainly in English medieval history.
sentences.zh: 这通常被视为一个转折点，在英格兰中世纪历史上尤其如此。

sentences.en: And the question is, was it?
sentences.zh: 问题是，真的是这样吗？

sentences.en: Well, that's what we're going to explore today, Dominic, because we have done two episodes on the Great Revolt, the Peasants' Revolt of 1381.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这就是我们今天要探讨的，多米尼克，因为我们已经做了两集关于1381年大起义、农民起义的节目。

sentences.en: But there are more tumultuous episodes in the reign of Richard II.
sentences.zh: 但在理查二世统治期间，还有更多动荡的插曲。

sentences.en: And we've given a massive spoiler alert as to what the most dramatic of all is, the deposition of Richard II.
sentences.zh: 我们已经对其中最戏剧性的一幕发出了剧烈剧透警告，那就是理查二世的废黜。

sentences.en: But as you say, the question is, how did Richard II come to be deposed?
sentences.zh: 但正如你所说，问题是，理查二世是如何沦落到被废黜的境地的？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: And how significant is it for the history of the 15th century, which will follow through?
sentences.zh: 这对于接下来15世纪的历史具有怎样的重大意义？

sentences.en: So Tom, just to recap for those people who are coming to the show after a big break or something, we're at the midpoint of the Hundred Years' War.
sentences.zh: 那么汤姆，简单回顾一下那些在经历漫长假期后回到节目的听众，我们正处于百年战争的中点。

sentences.en: Edward III, who was Richard II's predecessor, had had this absolutely glorious reign, lots of victors, Cressy, Poitier, and so on.
sentences.zh: 理查二世的前任爱德华三世度过了一个绝对辉煌的统治期，取得了许多胜利，如克雷西、普瓦捷等等。

sentences.en: But the English had been effectively forced back.
sentences.zh: 但英国人实际上已经被迫退守。

sentences.en: This is now halftime.
sentences.zh: 现在是中场休息了。

sentences.en: They're kind of not licking their wounds exactly.
sentences.zh: 他们算不上是在舔舐伤口。

sentences.en: Oh, they are a bit, I think.
sentences.zh: 哦，我想他们确实有点在舔舐伤口。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好吧。

sentences.en: They're in the dressing room and they've, you know, they've been hacked around and people are kind of trying to patch things up.
sentences.zh: 他们呆在更衣室里，你知道的，他们饱受摧残，人们正试图把事情收拾妥当。

sentences.en: But from the point of view of Richard II, the previous two episodes we did, the problem has been domestic and specifically the Peasants' Revolt,
sentences.zh: 但从理查二世的角度来看——我们做过的前两集节目——问题出在内政上，具体来说就是农民起义，

sentences.en: the Great Revolt, as it's called, in 1381.
sentences.zh: 即1381年的所谓大起义。

sentences.en: And let's just look at how that might have affected Richard.
sentences.zh: 让我们来看看这可能对理查产生了什么影响。

sentences.en: So he had stood on the Tower of London and he had seen London burning.
sentences.zh: 他曾站在伦敦塔上，目睹了伦敦在燃烧。

sentences.en: And I think it's probably not over-psychologizing to think that this must have imbued in him a kind of visceral dread of civic disorder.
sentences.zh: 我想，认为这必定在他心中灌输了一种对公民骚乱的本能恐惧，大概并不算是过度心理分析。

sentences.en: I think he's also only a young boy at this point.
sentences.zh: 我想此时他其实也只是个小男孩。

sentences.en: He's 14 years old.
sentences.zh: 他才14岁。

sentences.en: And it must have given him a feeling of impotence that policy is still basically being decided for him by the people who effectively have the reins of government in their hands.
sentences.zh: 这一定让他产生了一种无力感，因为政策基本上仍然是由那些实际掌握着政府大权的人为他决定的。

sentences.en: And yet the paradox is it gives him a massive sense of agency at the same time there, doesn't it?
sentences.zh: 然而矛盾的是，与此同时这又赋予了他一种巨大的自主意识，对吧？

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 绝对如此。

sentences.en: Because, as we described in the previous episode,
sentences.zh: 因为正如我们在上一集里描述的那样，

sentences.en: Richard is aware that as king, he has an incredible charisma, that the people love him.
sentences.zh: 理查意识到作为国王，他拥有令人难以置信的个人魅力，人民爱戴他。

sentences.en: They may hate his ministers, but they love him.
sentences.zh: 他们可能痛恨他的大臣，但他们爱他。

sentences.en: And this, of course, is also, I think, part of the swirl of influences that the Peasants' Revolt has on him.
sentences.zh: 当然，这也是我认为农民起义对他的各种影响交织的一部分。

sentences.en: So basically, the Peasants' Revolt bigs him up in his own mind.
sentences.zh: 所以基本上，农民起义让他在自己心中自我膨胀了。

sentences.en: It does.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: And it goes with the grain of the effect of his upbringing.
sentences.zh: 这与他成长环境的影响不谋而合。

sentences.en: He's not actually the only son of the Black Prince.
sentences.zh: 他其实并不是黑太子的独子。

sentences.en: So there'd been an elder brother, but he died in infancy.
sentences.zh: 他曾有一个哥哥，但在婴儿时期就夭折了。

sentences.en: The Black Prince, he'd had this glittering court in Bordeaux.
sentences.zh: 黑太子曾在波尔多建立过璀璨夺目的宫廷。

sentences.en: He'd then come back to die in Kennington, near what today is the Kennington Oval.
sentences.zh: 后来他回到肯宁顿去世，就在今天的肯宁顿椭圆球场附近。

sentences.en: And Richard, I think, growing up, would have absolutely lived with a consciousness of what a tremendous dash his father had displayed as a great lord in his court.
sentences.zh: 我认为理查在成长过程中，必定对他的父亲作为伟大的领主在其宫廷中展现出的非凡气魄有着清醒的认识。

sentences.en: And I think that it provides Richard, through his childhood, up to the Peasants' Revolt, and then in the years that follow, with a sense that he must uphold his dignity
sentences.zh: 我认为这为理查提供了一种信念：从他的童年、直到农民起义，再到随后的几年里，他都必须维护自己的尊严，

sentences.en: and that it's incredibly important to put on a good show.
sentences.zh: 而且展现出良好的风范是极其重要的。

sentences.en: Because more than their predecessors,
sentences.zh: 因为比起他们的前任，

sentences.en: Edward III and the Black Prince had been all about spectacle and glamour and chivalry and stuff.
sentences.zh: 爱德华三世和黑太子更看重壮观场面、迷人魅力和骑士精神之类的事物。

sentences.en: Is that right?
sentences.zh: 是这样吗？

sentences.en: Absolutely, yes.
sentences.zh: 当然，是的。

sentences.en: And of course, achievement.
sentences.zh: 当然还有功绩。

sentences.en: And there's a slight problem for Richard that he hasn't really achieved anything.
sentences.zh: 对理查来说有个小问题，那就是他其实还没有取得过任何功绩。

sentences.en: And so I think that that's why perhaps he puts an extra premium on the dignity that he hasn't won it, but he has been given it by God as he sees it.
sentences.zh: 所以我想，这也许就是为什么他格外看重尊严——这份尊严并非他赢得的，而是正如他所见，由上帝赐予他的。

sentences.en: So in Shakespeare's play, there's this famous couplet, not all the waters in the rough road sea can wash the balm off from an anointed king.
sentences.zh: 所以在莎士比亚的戏剧中，有这样一幅著名的对联：纵使粗暴大海的千层海水，也无法洗去受膏君王身上的圣油。

sentences.en: And the fact that Richard is anointed and that he has succeeded to the throne by right is incredibly important to him.
sentences.zh: 理查是受膏者，且他是凭正统继承王位，这一事实对他来说极其重要。

sentences.en: And in the previous episode, we talked about how Edward the Confessor is Richard's great patron.
sentences.zh: 在上一集中，我们讨论了忏悔者爱德华如何成为理查的伟大守护神。

sentences.en: Richard has been crowned and anointed in Westminster Abbey, the shrine built by Edward the Confessor.
sentences.zh: 理查在威斯敏斯特教堂加冕并接受涂油，这座圣地正是由忏悔者爱德华修建的。

sentences.en: And Richard feels that this has set him aside from other mortals, that he, in a sense, is separate from his subjects.
sentences.zh: 理查觉得这使他区别于其他凡人，从某种意义上说，他独立于他的臣民之外。

sentences.en: And the key detail, I mean, it's kind of announced by the Archbishop of Canterbury shortly after Richard had been crowned, that he's king not by election, nor by any such path,
sentences.zh: 而关键的细节——我是说，在理查加冕后不久，坎特伯雷大主教就宣布了这一点——他成为国王不是通过选举，也不是通过任何此类途径，

sentences.en: but by lawful right of succession.
sentences.zh: 而是通过合法的继承权。

sentences.en: So that's the key.
sentences.zh: 所以这就是关键所在。

sentences.en: But why does that make him different from previous monarchs, of whom the same could be said?
sentences.zh: 但为什么这使他与以往的君主有所不同呢？对于以往的君主同样可以说出这样的话。

sentences.en: It absolutely doesn't.
sentences.zh: 完全没有不同。

sentences.en: But for Richard,
sentences.zh: 但对于理查而言，

sentences.en: Edward III had demonstrated what a great king he was through military achievement.
sentences.zh: 爱德华三世通过军事成就证明了自己是一位伟大的国王。

sentences.en: Richard is a boy, and as he's growing up, therefore he needs to emphasize why he has the right to take over the reins of power.
sentences.zh: 理查还是个男孩，随着他逐渐长大，他因此需要强调他为什么有权接掌权力。

sentences.en: And this right is basically because God wants him to be king.
sentences.zh: 而这种权利基本上是因为上帝希望他成为国王。

sentences.en: He is the rightful heir to his grandfather.
sentences.zh: 他是他祖父的正统继承人。

sentences.en: You also have this devotion to kind of display and show, which is also a crucial part of Richard's character.
sentences.zh: 你还会发现他对展示和炫耀有一种热爱，这也是理查性格中至关重要的一部分。

sentences.en: So, I mean, he's not in any way wussy.
sentences.zh: 所以，我的意思是，他一点也不娘娘腔。

sentences.en: He's very kind of strong, loves hunting, in that sense, very much his father's son.
sentences.zh: 他非常强壮，热爱打猎，从这个意义上说，他非常像他的父亲。

sentences.en: But I think he has a slight kind of metrosexual quality.
sentences.zh: 但我认为他有一种轻微的都市美男气质。

sentences.en: Well, he's often played that way in Shakespeare's playwright.
sentences.zh: 好吧，他在莎士比亚的剧作中通常就是这样被扮演的。

sentences.en: So the classic one that people may have seen is the TV version with David Tennant, where Tennant has kind of very, very long hair and he's very fae and a bit camp.
sentences.zh: 人们可能看过的经典版本是带有大卫·田纳特的那部电视剧，田纳特留着非常非常长的头发，显得非常柔美且略带矫揉造作。

sentences.en: And that's how people normally think of Richard II, right?
sentences.zh: 人们通常就是这样看待理查二世的，对吧？

sentences.en: Well...
They get him mixed up with Edward II and they say, oh, he's a bit camp and foppish.
sentences.zh: 他们把他和爱德华二世混淆了，然后说，噢，他有点矫揉造作又爱讲究。

sentences.en: I mean, it's not entirely inaccurate.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这并非完全不准确。

sentences.en: So the Monk of Eveship reports that Richard does have kind of long, blonde hair, a very pale complexion, and says that his features are feminine.
sentences.zh: 伊夫舍姆的修道士记载说，理查确实留着长长的金发，脸色非常苍白，并说他的五官带有女性特征。

sentences.en: And a lot of the paintings he is given quite kind of feminine features.
sentences.zh: 在许多画像中，他也被赋予了相当具有女性特征的面容。

sentences.en: So that must have been
sentences.zh: 所以这必定是

sentences.en: Richard's own commission.
sentences.zh: 理查自己的委托定制。

sentences.en: So that's not the same as Roman historians saying of emperors, oh, they bleach their hair and they shave their legs with shells or whatever, those kinds of things.
sentences.zh: 所以这跟罗马历史学家评价皇帝时说“噢，他们用贝壳漂白头发、刮腿毛”之类的完全不同。

sentences.en: No.
sentences.zh: 不。

sentences.en: This isn't propaganda dissing him.
sentences.zh: 这不是在抹黑他的政治宣传。

sentences.en: No, quite the contrary.
sentences.zh: 不，恰恰相反。

sentences.en: I think it's Richard kind of portraying himself.
sentences.zh: 我认为这是理查在塑造他自己的形象。

sentences.en: Essentially, I mean, he's a dedicated follower of fashion.
sentences.zh: 本质上讲，他是一个狂热的时尚追随者。

sentences.en: He's very, very stylish.
sentences.zh: 他非常、非常时髦。

sentences.en: He loves his clothes.
sentences.zh: 他热爱他的衣服。

sentences.en: I mean, he rather despises the French king,
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他相当鄙视法国国王

sentences.en: Charles VI.
sentences.zh: 查理六世。

sentences.en: They go and have a summit in 1396 and the French king wears the same robe three days in succession.
sentences.zh: 他们在1396年举行了一次峰会，法国国王连续三天穿同一件长袍。

sentences.en: And Richard regards this with absolute contempt.
sentences.zh: 而理查对此报以绝对的蔑视。

sentences.en: So he's kind of endlessly, you know, one day he's wearing a magnificent gown of white velvet and red sleeves and the next an outfit of blue velvet decorated with gold.
sentences.zh: 所以他总是没完没了地——你知道的，今天穿着一件配有红色衣袖的华丽白丝绒长袍，明天又换上一套饰有黄金的蓝色丝绒服饰。

sentences.en: His table is the best in Europe, most extravagant.
sentences.zh: 他的餐桌是欧洲最好的，也是最奢华的。

sentences.en: Lots of spices, lots of kind of ducks inside, turkeys inside whatever.
sentences.zh: 有大量的香料，里面塞满了各种鸭子、火鸡之类的东西。

sentences.en: Turduckens.
sentences.zh: 多重夹馅烤禽。

sentences.en: Turduckens, all that kind of thing.
sentences.zh: 多重夹馅烤禽，诸如此类的一切。

sentences.en: He's also the first
sentences.zh: 他也是第一个

sentences.en: English king to use a fork.
sentences.zh: 使用叉子的英格兰国王。

sentences.en: Oh, that's poor.
sentences.zh: 噢，那可真糟糕。

sentences.en: And supposedly to use a handkerchief.
sentences.zh: 据说他还是第一个使用手帕的人。

sentences.en: I don't approve of either of those innovations.
sentences.zh: 这两项革新我都不赞同。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: So you as a rugged son of the Shires might regard this with a measure of contempt.
sentences.zh: 所以你作为一个来自郡县的粗犷硬汉，可能会对此抱有一定的鄙视。

sentences.en: But Richard is doing it for political reasons.
sentences.zh: 但理查这样做是出于政治原因。

sentences.en: So it's, you know, again, it's just setting himself aside.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道的，这同样是为了让自己与众不同。

sentences.en: It's about making people appreciate that he is someone distinctive.
sentences.zh: 这是为了让人们意识到他是一个与众不同的人。

sentences.en: So that's what it's all about.
sentences.zh: 这就是这一切的意义所在。

sentences.en: But you can imagine that this must make him a bit of a nightmare to handle as he's growing up.
sentences.zh: 但你可以想象，随着他逐渐长大，这一定让他成了一个极其难缠的头疼人物。

sentences.en: So he's a bit of a diva, basically.
sentences.zh: 所以他基本上算是个有点大牌的人。

sentences.en: Bit of a diva.
sentences.zh: 有点大牌。

sentences.en: A bit of a diva.
sentences.zh: 有点大牌派头。

sentences.en: Very, very self-conscious.
sentences.zh: 非常、非常有自我意识。

sentences.en: Very, very stylish.
sentences.zh: 非常、非常时髦。

sentences.en: Probably an awkward teenager to have around.
sentences.zh: 身边带着他大概是个令人头疼的青少年。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: And I think even more so when on the 6th of January
sentences.zh: 我认为更是如此，在1383年

sentences.en: 1383, he celebrates his 16th birthday, comes of age, and he's now at the same age as the Black Prince was when he won his Spurs at Cressy.
sentences.zh: 1月6日，他庆祝了自己的16岁生日，正式成年，而此时他的年龄与黑太子在克雷西赢得金马刺时的年龄一样大。

sentences.en: Tom, I don't want to say what everybody's thinking, but you're Richard II and I'm Henry Bolingbroke.
sentences.zh: 汤姆，我不想说出大家心里都在想的事，但你是理查二世，而我是亨利·博林布鲁克。

sentences.en: I mean,
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，

sentences.en: I'm just putting that out there.
sentences.zh: 我只是随口一提。

sentences.en: I think that this is a parallel that we may reprise.
sentences.zh: 我认为这是一个我们可能会重演的平行故事。

sentences.en: So Richard still has lots of uncles on the scene, specifically two.
sentences.zh: 所以理查的身边依然有很多叔父，具体来说是两位。

sentences.en: So John Gaunt, who we mentioned, very, very unpopular with the rebels in London who trashed his palace.
sentences.zh: 我们提到过的约翰·冈特，在伦敦的叛乱分子中非常、非常不受欢迎，他们砸毁了他的宫殿。

sentences.en: But he remains, by miles, the richest and most powerful figure in England.
sentences.zh: 但他依然是英格兰无可争议、最富有、最有权势的人物。

sentences.en: And he's suspected of aspiring to the throne.
sentences.zh: 而且他被怀疑觊觎王位。

sentences.en: This is unfair, actually.
sentences.zh: 这其实挺不公平的。

sentences.en: He's very, very loyal to his nephew, his much-loved brother's son.
sentences.zh: 他对他的侄子，也就是他深受爱戴的兄弟的儿子，非常非常忠诚。

sentences.en: And also we have on the scene
sentences.zh: 同时我们也在现场看到了

sentences.en: Thomas of Woodstock, who had been, you remember in the previous episode, he'd been dashing off to Brittany periodically and not doing very well and then coming back.
sentences.zh: 伍德斯托克的托马斯，大家还记得在上集里，他曾时不时地冲去布列塔尼，虽然战绩不佳却又折返。

sentences.en: And he has now been elevated to a dukedom, the Duke of Gloucester.
sentences.zh: 他现在已经被册封为公爵，即格洛斯特公爵。

sentences.en: So these are the two guys who feel that basically they should be running the country.
sentences.zh: 所以这两个人觉得自己基本上才应该治理这个国家。

sentences.en: The problem is
sentences.zh: 问题在于

sentences.en: Richard is very much the kind of king who has favourites.
sentences.zh: 理查是一个非常喜欢任用宠臣的国王。

sentences.en: So this is something that Edward II,
sentences.zh: 所以这种情况，也就是爱德华二世——

sentences.en: Edward III's father, had been notorious for his favourites.
sentences.zh: 也就是爱德华三世的父亲——以重用宠臣而臭名昭著。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And it had ended up kind of bringing him down.
sentences.zh: 而这也最终导致了他的垮台。

sentences.en: Richard, he's got a kind of a gang of friends who he favours very, very strongly.
sentences.zh: 理查呢，他有一帮非常非常偏爱的朋友。

sentences.en: So among them, there is a guy called Michael de la Pole, who is from a family of wool merchants from Hull.
sentences.zh: 在他们当中，有一个叫迈克尔·德·拉·波尔的人，他来自赫尔的一个羊毛商家庭。

sentences.en: Glamorous.
sentences.zh: 真风光啊。

sentences.en: Not the kind of person who John of Gaunt necessarily might approve of.
sentences.zh: 这可未必是冈特的约翰所能看得上的人。

sentences.en: But Richard loves him and he sends him off on all kinds of diplomatic missions.
sentences.zh: 但理查很喜欢他，并派他去执行各种外交使命。

sentences.en: And it's Michael de la Pole who finds him a very glamorous bride in the form of Anne of Bohemia, she's called.
sentences.zh: 正是迈克尔·德·拉·波尔为他物色了一位十分耀眼的新娘，名叫波西米亚的安妮。

sentences.en: So she's the daughter of the Holy Roman Emperor.
sentences.zh: 所以她是神圣罗马帝国的女儿。

sentences.en: He's brought over.
sentences.zh: 他被迎娶过来了。

sentences.en: They marry.
sentences.zh: 他们结婚了。

sentences.en: Very happy marriage, although they don't have children.
sentences.zh: 这是一桩非常幸福的婚姻，尽管他们没有孩子。

sentences.en: And as a reward for this,
sentences.zh: 为了表彰这一点，

sentences.en: Michael de la Pole is first appointed
sentences.zh: 迈克尔·德·拉·波尔先是被任命为

sentences.en: Chancellor and then in 1385,
sentences.zh: 大法官，随后在1385年，

sentences.en: Richard makes him the Earl of Suffolk.
sentences.zh: 理查封他为萨福克伯爵。

sentences.en: So this is a guy who is on the make.
sentences.zh: 所以这是一个平步青云的人。

sentences.en: Are they the same age?
sentences.zh: 他们俩同龄吗？

sentences.en: He's a little bit older.
sentences.zh: 他稍微大一点。

sentences.en: No, he's older.
sentences.zh: 不，他年纪更大。

sentences.en: And also older is a guy called
sentences.zh: 同样年长的人还有一个叫

sentences.en: Simon Burley.
sentences.zh: 西蒙·伯利。

sentences.en: He was Richard's tutor, a very good friend of the Black Prince, had been involved again in the marriage negotiations and is seen by everyone as being incredibly common.
sentences.zh: 他是理查的导师，黑太子的挚友，曾再次参与婚姻谈判，在所有人眼中显得极其粗俗。

sentences.en: So all the nobles regard him as beyond vulgar.
sentences.zh: 因此，所有的贵族都认为他粗鄙不堪。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So Michael de la Pole and Simon Burley are older, but there is one guy in particular who is Richard's age, whom he adores, his best friend, who is a guy called Robert de Vere,
sentences.zh: 所以迈克尔·德·拉·波尔和西蒙·伯利年纪较大，但有一个人与理查同龄，备受他的宠爱，可以说是他最好的朋友，这个人叫罗伯特·德·韦尔，

sentences.en: the Earl of Oxford.
sentences.zh: 牛津伯爵。

sentences.en: And Robert de Vere, I mean, that's a very, very epicene favourite kind of name.
sentences.zh: 而且罗伯特·德·韦尔，我的意思是，这名字听起来就有一种非常雌雄同体的宠臣风范。

sentences.en: And there are people who suggest that Richard and de Vere are lovers.
sentences.zh: 有人暗示理查和德·韦尔是一对恋人。

sentences.en: I mean, they may have been, we don't know, but actually de Vere is a massive womaniser.
sentences.zh: 我是说，他们可能曾经是，我们不得而知，但实际上德·韦尔是个不折不扣的大仲马。

sentences.en: So there's a big scandal where he runs off with his wife's lady-in-waiting, which is...
sentences.zh: 所以曾发生过一桩大丑闻，他与妻子的宫廷女侍私奔了，这……

sentences.en: That's not good.
sentences.zh: 这可不太好。

sentences.en: Yeah, very, very poor behaviour.
sentences.zh: 对，行为非常非常恶劣。

sentences.en: And Richard lavishes him with all kinds of titles.
sentences.zh: 而理查对他各种封爵赏赐。

sentences.en: So he's the first guy to be made a Marquis in English history.
sentences.zh: 所以他是英国历史上第一个被封为侯爵的人。

sentences.en: He's made the Marquis of Dublin.
sentences.zh: 他被封为都柏林侯爵。

sentences.en: Marquis of Dublin.
sentences.zh: 都柏林侯爵。

sentences.en: And why Marquis?
sentences.zh: 为什么是侯爵？

sentences.en: Is this because it's a fancy title and it's a little bit different and...
sentences.zh: 是因为这是一个时髦的头衔，有点与众不同，而且……

sentences.en: A little bit posh, a little bit foreign.
sentences.zh: 有点高档，有点异国情调。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And then in 1386, he gets made the Duke of Ireland, which is...
sentences.zh: 然后在1386年，他被册封为爱尔兰公爵，这……

sentences.en: The Duke of Ireland.
sentences.zh: 爱尔兰公爵。

sentences.en: I didn't know such a title existed.
sentences.zh: 我以前都不知道还有这种头衔。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: So that's nice for our Irish listeners.
sentences.zh: 所以这对我们的爱尔兰听众来说挺不错的。

sentences.en: And so you can imagine that this is really, really pissing off all the great magnets.
sentences.zh: 所以你可以想象，这真的彻底惹恼了所有的显赫权贵。

sentences.en: So the royal uncles, but also leading noblemans.
sentences.zh: 也就是皇室叔父们，还有领头的贵族们。

sentences.en: You've got the Earl of Warwick.
sentences.zh: 比如沃里克伯爵。

sentences.en: You've got the Earl of Arundel.
sentences.zh: 比如阿伦黛尔伯爵。

sentences.en: They're cross about this.
sentences.zh: 他们对此很不爽。

sentences.en: And this obviously matters because Richard II, as king, you know, you can go on about his anointing and how he's appointed by God and all this kind of stuff, but he cannot rule
sentences.zh: 这显然很重要，因为理查二世作为国王，你知道的，你可以喋喋不休地谈论他的涂圣油仪式、他是如何受命于天诸如此类的事情，但他如果没有权贵们的支持，

sentences.en: without the backing of the magnets.
sentences.zh: 是根本无法统治的。

sentences.en: And I think he's...
sentences.zh: 而且我觉得他……

sentences.en: You know,
sentences.zh: 你知道的，

sentences.en: Edward III, he had been a lad and the magnets are basically lads and it had been brilliant.
sentences.zh: 爱德华三世以前也是个毛头小伙子，权贵们基本上也都是些小伙子，那时候一切都棒极了。

sentences.en: So you compared me to Richard II.
sentences.zh: 所以你拿我和理查二世做比较。

sentences.en: I mean, it's a bit like when we were on our tour of Australia, you and Theo and Dom chatting about the Champions League
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这有点像我们在澳大利亚巡演时，你、西奥和多姆在聊欧冠

sentences.en: quarterfinals in whatever,
sentences.zh: 四分之一决赛，不管那是哪一年，

sentences.en: 2007, and I'm sitting there.
sentences.zh: 2007年，而我正坐在那儿。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: So basically,
sentences.zh: 所以基本上，

sentences.en: Richard II is not hanging out with the magnets talking about the Champions League.
sentences.zh: 理查二世可不是那种会跟权贵们一起闲聊欧冠的人。

sentences.en: He's sitting there with his fork and his handkerchief.
sentences.zh: 他只会拿着叉子和手帕坐在那儿。

sentences.en: Thinking about Christianity.
sentences.zh: 思考着基督教。

sentences.en: Talking about the history of Christianity.
sentences.zh: 谈论着基督教的历史。

sentences.en: All that kind of stuff.
sentences.zh: 诸如此类的事情。

sentences.en: And so this means that tensions are created and tensions are further created by the fact that the Hundred Years' War, which is still rumbling on, it isn't going well.
sentences.zh: 这就意味着矛盾正在产生，而百年战争至今仍在持续且进展不顺，这也进一步加剧了紧张局势。

sentences.en: Richard II isn't a very good war leader.
sentences.zh: 理查二世并不是一个出色的军事统帅。

sentences.en: The French are massing a huge army on the Channel.
sentences.zh: 法国人在海峡集结了庞大的军队。

sentences.en: Richard goes off to try and defeat the Scots.
sentences.zh: 理查御驾亲征试图击败苏格兰人。

sentences.en: That doesn't go well either.
sentences.zh: 结果也不太顺利。

sentences.en: And the result is that basically the number of people whom Richard can rely on is shrinking and shrinking and shrinking the whole time.
sentences.zh: 其结果就是，理查能够依靠的人变得越来越少，一直在不断缩减。

sentences.en: And this crisis is then accelerated by two developments in 1386.
sentences.zh: 而1386发生的两起事件，让这场危机进一步加速恶化。

sentences.en: Just before you get on to those two developments,
sentences.zh: 在你讲到那两件事之前，

sentences.en: Tom, a quick question for you.
sentences.zh: 汤姆，我有个简单的问题想问你。

sentences.en: An obvious question.
sentences.zh: 一个显而易见的问题。

sentences.en: Everything you were describing about Richard II is kind of medieval politics 101.
sentences.zh: 你刚才对理查二世的所有描述，基本上就是中世纪政治的入门必修课。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: You know, manage your magnates, be nice to the big power brokers, all that stuff.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，驾驭你的权贵，对各大权力操纵者好一点，诸如此类。

sentences.en: And he has an example in his own family of Edward II.
sentences.zh: 而且他家族里就有爱德华二世这个前车之鉴。

sentences.en: Yeah, he does.
sentences.zh: 对，确实有。

sentences.en: Just two kings earlier, who'd made a terrible horlicks of this and ended up supposedly having an encounter with a red-hot poker.
sentences.zh: 就在仅仅两代之前的国王，把这事儿搞得一团糟，据说最后还遭遇了红热拨火棍的「亲密接触」。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: Although that probably didn't happen.
sentences.zh: 虽然那可能并没有发生过。

sentences.en: Why on earth does he not learn the lesson from that?
sentences.zh: 他到底为什么就不能从中吸取教训呢？

sentences.en: I mean, it's not that long ago.
sentences.zh: 我是说，这也没过去多久啊。

sentences.en: Because I think he doesn't know how else to rule.
sentences.zh: 因为我觉得他不知道还能怎么统治。

sentences.en: He's trying to rule as best he can.
sentences.zh: 他正竭尽所能地去统治。

sentences.en: And the fact that he starts to make some of the same mistakes that his great-grandfather had made is kind of irrelevant to him.
sentences.zh: 至于他开始犯下他曾祖父犯过的一些相同错误，对他来说其实并不重要。

sentences.en: He's not looking back to the example of Edward II.
sentences.zh: 他没有去回顾爱德华二世的榜样。

sentences.en: He's trying to do the best that he can.
sentences.zh: 他只是在尽自己最大的努力。

sentences.en: And the fact that he's replaying some of these mistakes, you know, it just points to certain structural deficiencies, I think, in royal government in the 14th century.
sentences.zh: 而他正在重蹈覆辙这件事，我认为，恰恰指出了14世纪王室统治中存在的某种结构性缺陷。

sentences.en: So it's a structural issue as much as it is a temperamental one, do you think?
sentences.zh: 所以你认为这既是一个结构性问题，也是一个性格问题？

sentences.en: I think it's a structural issue if you are not a successful war leader
sentences.zh: 我认为，如果你不是一个成功的军事统帅，

sentences.en: and if you lack the kind of easy charm that Edward III had had.
sentences.zh: 并且缺乏爱德华三世那种随和的魅力，它就是一个结构性问题。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好吧。

sentences.en: I think being a lad is a kind of requirement for being a successful medieval king.
sentences.zh: 我觉得当一个合格的中世纪国王，当个爱玩的小伙子算是一种硬性要求。

sentences.en: And that's why basically in 1386 two things happen that really accentuate the crisis.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么基本上在1386年发生了两件真正加剧危机的事情。

sentences.en: The first is that
sentences.zh: 首先是

sentences.en: John of Gaunt leaves England.
sentences.zh: 冈特的约翰离开英格兰。

sentences.en: Turned out to be for three years.
sentences.zh: 结果这一走就是三年。

sentences.en: He's gone off to Spain to try and make himself the king of Castile.
sentences.zh: 他去了西班牙，试图让自己成为卡斯蒂利亚国王。

sentences.en: So this is a kind of as you do.
sentences.zh: 所以这真是一种「不愧是你」的操作。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And this is a problem for Richard because John of Gaunt, you know, he's the greatest man in the kingdom and had been very supportive of his nephew.
sentences.zh: 这对理查来说是个问题，因为冈特的约翰，你知道的，他是王国里最伟大的人物，而且一直非常支持他的侄子。

sentences.en: And now he's gone.
sentences.zh: 而现在他走了。

sentences.en: There is a kind of void at the center.
sentences.zh: 权力中心出现了一种真空。

sentences.en: There is also an absolutely massive invasion scare.
sentences.zh: 同时还存在着极其巨大的入侵恐慌。

sentences.en: So you have 30,000 men massed on the French coaSt.
sentences.zh: 法国海岸集结了三万大军。

sentences.en: A contemporary chronicler compares it to the Greek army which had destroyed Troy, which is, you know, not the kind of detail that you want.
sentences.zh: 一位当代的编年史家将其比作摧毁特洛伊的希腊军队，这可不是你希望听到的细节。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: You know, this is up there with the Spanish Armada and Napoleon in 1805 as one of the great invasion scares.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，这完全可以和西班牙无敌舰队以及1805年的拿破仑相提并论，堪称历史上几次大举入侵恐慌之一。

sentences.en: I mean, we don't remember it because in the event it doesn't happen.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我们记不住它，是因为后来它并没有发生。

sentences.en: But at the time it causes massive panic.
sentences.zh: 但在当时，它引发了极大的恐慌。

sentences.en: And so Michael de la Pole, who is chancellor, he's the guy who's charged with raising the money that would enable England to see this threat off.
sentences.zh: 因此，身为主计长的迈克尔·德·拉·波尔，他负责筹集资金，以便让英格兰能够抵御这场威胁。

sentences.en: And so he summons Parliament.
sentences.zh: 于是他召集了议会。

sentences.en: Parliament is furious because Parliament is getting fed up with being summoned and asked for money.
sentences.zh: 议会对此愤怒不已，因为议会已经厌倦了一次次被召集并被索要钱财。

sentences.en: And the MPs demand that Richard sacks de la Pole.
sentences.zh: 下议院的议员们要求理查撤职德·拉·波尔。

sentences.en: And Richard has a hissy fit about this and famously says that he would not dismiss so much as a kitchen scullion from office at the request of, you know, mere commoners.
sentences.zh: 理查为此大发雷霆，并说出了那句名言：哪怕只是为了区区平民的请求，他也不会罢免一个厨房里的洗碗杂役。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好吧。

sentences.en: And this is when
sentences.zh: 也就是在这个时候，

sentences.en: Gloucester and the Earl of Arundel, they go to Richard and they specifically remind him of the fate of Edward II.
sentences.zh: 格洛斯特和阿伦黛尔伯爵去见了理查，并特意提醒了他爱德华二世的悲惨下场。

sentences.en: They say, listen, you know, you are skirting with danger here.
sentences.zh: 他们说，听着，你知道的，你这是在玩火。

sentences.en: And Richard is sufficiently alarmed at this that he agrees to dismiss de la Pole.
sentences.zh: 理查对此感到足够惊恐，于是同意罢免德·拉·波尔。

sentences.en: So it's a victory for Parliament and it's a victory for the Duke of Gloucester.
sentences.zh: 所以这是议会的胜利，也是格洛斯特公爵的胜利。

sentences.en: For the big magnates, the big landowners, yeah.
sentences.zh: 对于大权贵、大地主们来说，是的。

sentences.en: And further humiliations are heaped on Richard.
sentences.zh: 更多的羞辱接踵而至，全数倾倒在理查头上。

sentences.en: So de la Pole is impeached so he's charged by Parliament on charges of negligence and of embezzlement but everyone knows that it's really
sentences.zh: 因此德·拉·波尔遭到弹劾，他被议会指控玩忽职守和挪用公款，但大家都知道，真正遭到攻击的其实是

sentences.en: Richard himself who is being attacked.
sentences.zh: 理查本人。

sentences.en: And Parliament sets up a council that has powers to kind of go through all the royal accounts to check that money hasn't been embezzled and this kind of Parliamentary
sentences.zh: 议会成立了一个委员会，拥有查阅所有皇家账目的权力，以核实资金没有被挪用，这种议会性质的

sentences.en: Commission by November 1386 is basically in charge of the entire government and it's an incredible humiliation.
sentences.zh: 委员会在1386年11月基本上掌控了整个政府，这真是一场难以置信的羞辱。
